title: Scheme-theoretic union of two closed subschemes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $i':Z'\to X$, $i'':Z''\to X$ be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaves $\mathcal I'=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'})$ and $\mathcal I''=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i''_*\mathcal O_{Z''})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Then $\mathcal I'\cap\mathcal I''$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$; let $i''':Z'''\to X$ be the closed immersion it defines (the *scheme-theoretic union* $Z'\cup Z''$; on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] where $Z'\cap U$, $Z''\cap U$ are cut out by ideals $I,J\subseteq A$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(I\cap J))\to\operatorname{Spec}A$). Then: (a) the underlying set $i'''(Z''')$ equals $i'(Z')\cup i''(Z'')$; (b) there are closed immersions $a':Z'\to Z'''$ and $a'':Z''\to Z'''$ with $i'''\circ a'=i'$ and $i'''\circ a''=i''$.

proof.text: Let I be the infimum of the two kernel ideal sheaves, using [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-intersection]. The closed subscheme is I.subscheme with its canonical inclusion. The closed-immersion instance and IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι give its closedness and kernel, as in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]. Apply the proved source lemma IdealSheafData.isPullback_subschemeCover_map (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.Subscheme) to identify every affine chart with the pullback of the quotient spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: The intersection I and the product of the two kernels have equal radicals: IdealSheafData.radical_inf and radical_mul both give the infimum of their radicals. Rewriting by support_radical shows their supports agree. Mathlib IdealSheafData.support_mul, the support calculation in [lem-weil-pbc-product-ideal-closed-subscheme-union], gives the union of the two kernel supports. IdealSheafData.range_subschemeι gives the image of the constructed inclusion. As in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-image-zero-locus], Hom.support_ker identifies each original kernel support with the closure of its image. The original immersions have closed images, so these closures are their images. Coercion of the supremum of closed subsets is set union, yielding the required equality globally.

proof.text: By ker_subschemeι, the kernel of the constructed closed immersion is I. The inequalities inf_le_left and inf_le_right therefore satisfy the hypotheses of IsClosedImmersion.lift, the factorization in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion]. For each original immersion take that lift; lift_fac supplies its equation over X. Transport the closed-immersion instance of the original immersion along this equation, and apply IsClosedImmersion.of_comp_isClosedImmersion to prove that the factor itself is a closed immersion.

lean.statement: theorem scheme_theoretic_union {X Z' Z'' : Scheme.{u}} (i' : Z' ⟶ X) (i'' : Z'' ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i'] [IsClosedImmersion i''] : IsClosedImmersion (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subschemeι ∧ (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subschemeι.ker = i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker ∧ (∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsPullback ((i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subschemeCover.f U) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).ideal U)))) (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subschemeι U.2.fromSpec) ∧ Set.range (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subschemeι.base = Set.range i'.base ∪ Set.range i''.base ∧ (∃ a' : Z' ⟶ (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subscheme, IsClosedImmersion a' ∧ a' ≫ (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subschemeι = i') ∧ (∃ a'' : Z'' ⟶ (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subscheme, IsClosedImmersion a'' ∧ a'' ≫ (i'.ker ⊓ i''.ker).subschemeι = i'')
